text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Municipal elections pose a headache for all parties. Seventy-nine people are nominated as mayors and more than 1,000 as municipal councillors.
- Man considered missing for 15 years turns up in a Greek jail.
- Police find another arms cache close to Limassol.
- "Come and get us," says extremist Grey Wolves to Attorney-General Alecos Markides, who wants their leader's arrest on suspicion of murder.
- Cyprus Broadcasting Corporation is unable to pay its wages bill.
- Nurses to go ahead with strike.
- Communist party Akel proceeds to victory in December's municipal elections.
- The Western European Union has expressed concern that the accession of a divided Cyprus to the European Union could spark a crisis between the EU and Turkey.
- Parents who have children in pre-school will not allow the child of an Aids carrier to go to the same school.
- The government hopes to get 120 million pounds in tax for the defence fund in 1997.
- Municipal elections enter their final hurdle.
- (Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf) Denktash seeks a debate on confidence building measures with (President Glafcos) Clerides.
- Cyprus Broadcasting Corporation seeks a new handout from the taxpayer to solve its financial problems.
